typedef enum {
	PROTOBUF_C_TYPE_INT32,      /**< int32 */
	PROTOBUF_C_TYPE_SINT32,     /**< signed int32 */
	PROTOBUF_C_TYPE_SFIXED32,   /**< signed int32 (4 bytes) */
	PROTOBUF_C_TYPE_INT64,      /**< int64 */
	PROTOBUF_C_TYPE_SINT64,     /**< signed int64 */
	PROTOBUF_C_TYPE_SFIXED64,   /**< signed int64 (8 bytes) */
	PROTOBUF_C_TYPE_UINT32,     /**< unsigned int32 */
	PROTOBUF_C_TYPE_FIXED32,    /**< unsigned int32 (4 bytes) */
	PROTOBUF_C_TYPE_UINT64,     /**< unsigned int64 */
	PROTOBUF_C_TYPE_FIXED64,    /**< unsigned int64 (8 bytes) */
	PROTOBUF_C_TYPE_FLOAT,      /**< float */
	PROTOBUF_C_TYPE_DOUBLE,     /**< double */
	PROTOBUF_C_TYPE_BOOL,       /**< boolean */
	PROTOBUF_C_TYPE_ENUM,       /**< enumerated type */
	PROTOBUF_C_TYPE_STRING,     /**< UTF-8 or ASCII string */
	PROTOBUF_C_TYPE_BYTES,      /**< arbitrary byte sequence */
	PROTOBUF_C_TYPE_MESSAGE,    /**< nested message */
} ProtobufCType;

Abstract append-only sink used by pack_to_buffer; subclass by embedding as first member and providing append().

Helper for mostly-consecutive integer key lookups by storing ranges and original indices.
Base header shared by all generated message structs; carries descriptor and unknown-field storage.
Runtime descriptor for a message type: names, size, fields, lookup structures, and init function pointer.
Represents a field encountered on the wire not known to the descriptor, preserving tag, wire type, and raw bytes.

functions.name: protobuf_c_version
functions.description: Returns the version string of the protobuf-c library that the binary is linked against. Use to display or compare runtime library version.

functions.name: protobuf_c_version_number
functions.description: Returns the version of the linked protobuf-c library encoded as (MAJOR*1e6 + MINOR*1e3 + PATCH). Useful for numeric comparisons at runtime.

functions.name: protobuf_c_enum_descriptor_get_value_by_name
functions.description: Looks up an enum value in an enum descriptor by its name string and returns its ProtobufCEnumValue; returns NULL if not found or when the descriptor was generated with optimize_for = CODE_SIZE.
requirements: desc must point to a valid ProtobufCEnumDescriptor.
name must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string matching an enum value's name.
Caller must handle a NULL return (value not found or CODE_SIZE build).

functions.name: protobuf_c_enum_descriptor_get_value
functions.description: Looks up an enum value in an enum descriptor by its numeric value and returns its ProtobufCEnumValue; returns NULL if not found.
requirements: desc must point to a valid ProtobufCEnumDescriptor.
Caller must handle a NULL return when the numeric value is not present.

functions.name: protobuf_c_message_descriptor_get_field_by_name
functions.description: Looks up a field in a message descriptor by field name and returns its descriptor; returns NULL if not found or when generated with optimize_for = CODE_SIZE.
requirements: desc must point to a valid ProtobufCMessageDescriptor.
name must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string naming a field.
Caller must handle a NULL return (field not found or CODE_SIZE build).

functions.name: protobuf_c_message_descriptor_get_field
functions.description: Looks up a field in a message descriptor by its tag number and returns its descriptor; returns NULL if not found.
requirements: desc must point to a valid ProtobufCMessageDescriptor.
Caller must handle a NULL return when the tag number is not present.

functions.name: protobuf_c_message_get_packed_size
functions.description: Computes the number of bytes needed to serialize the given message. Use this before allocating the output buffer for packing.
requirements: message must point to a valid, initialized message of the correct type for its descriptor (uninitialized messages cannot be processed).

functions.name: protobuf_c_message_pack
functions.description: Serializes a message into a caller-provided buffer. Returns the number of bytes written. The buffer must be large enough, typically sized using protobuf_c_message_get_packed_size().
requirements: message must point to a valid, initialized message.
out must point to a writable buffer with capacity >= protobuf_c_message_get_packed_size(message).
Caller must allocate and manage the lifetime of the out buffer.

functions.name: protobuf_c_message_pack_to_buffer
functions.description: Serializes a message and streams the bytes to a virtual buffer by repeatedly invoking its append method. Returns the number of bytes passed to the buffer.
requirements: message must point to a valid, initialized message.
buffer must point to a valid ProtobufCBuffer whose append callback is set and able to consume len bytes per call.
The provided buffer implementation must handle any allocation or I/O errors internally (API provides no error return).

functions.name: protobuf_c_message_unpack
functions.signature: ProtobufCMessage *protobuf_c_message_unpack(const ProtobufCMessageDescriptor *descriptor, ProtobufCAllocator *allocator, size_t len, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Parses a serialized message (data,len) using the given descriptor and returns a newly allocated in-memory message. The allocator may be NULL to use the default. Returns NULL on parse or allocation error.
requirements: descriptor must point to the correct ProtobufCMessageDescriptor for the serialized data.
data must point to at least len bytes of the serialized message (data may be NULL only if len is 0).
allocator may be NULL to use the default allocator; otherwise it must point to a valid ProtobufCAllocator with alloc/free functions.
On success, the returned message must be freed with protobuf_c_message_free_unpacked() using the same allocator pointer that was provided to unpack.

functions.name: protobuf_c_message_free_unpacked
functions.description: Frees a message previously returned by protobuf_c_message_unpack(). Passing NULL for message is allowed and is a no-op. The allocator should match the one used for unpack.
requirements: message may be NULL; if non-NULL it must have been obtained from protobuf_c_message_unpack() for the same descriptor.
allocator may be NULL to use the default allocator; otherwise it must match the allocator used during unpacking.

functions.name: protobuf_c_message_check
functions.description: Validates a message tree, ensuring all required fields are present and recursively validating nested messages. Returns TRUE for valid, FALSE otherwise.
requirements: Input must point to a valid, initialized message consistent with its descriptor.

functions.name: protobuf_c_message_init
functions.description: Initializes a message instance for the given descriptor, setting the descriptor and default values so it can be processed by protobuf-c APIs. Use on stack- or heap-allocated storage before packing or checking.
requirements: descriptor must point to a valid ProtobufCMessageDescriptor.
message must point to writable storage of size at least descriptor->sizeof_message.
Must be called before using the message with other protobuf-c APIs if the object was not statically initialized.

functions.name: protobuf_c_service_destroy
functions.description: Destroys/frees a service instance. Typically used for services created by generated or custom code.
requirements: service must point to a valid ProtobufCService initialized with a descriptor and destroy function.

functions.name: protobuf_c_service_descriptor_get_method_by_name
functions.description: Looks up a method in a service descriptor by name and returns its descriptor; returns NULL if not found or when generated with optimize_for = CODE_SIZE.
requirements: desc must point to a valid ProtobufCServiceDescriptor.
name must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string naming a method.
Caller must handle a NULL return (method not found or CODE_SIZE build).

functions.name: protobuf_c_buffer_simple_append
functions.signature: void protobuf_c_buffer_simple_append(ProtobufCBuffer *buffer, size_t len, const unsigned char *data);
functions.description: Append callback implementation for ProtobufCBufferSimple. Grows the simple buffer as needed and copies len bytes from data into the buffer.
requirements: buffer must actually point to a ProtobufCBufferSimple instance (cast to its base).
If len > 0, data must point to at least len bytes to read.
The ProtobufCBufferSimple must have been initialized (e.g., via PROTOBUF_C_BUFFER_SIMPLE_INIT).

functions.name: protobuf_c_service_generated_init
functions.description: Initializes a ProtobufCService with a descriptor and destroy callback. Intended for use by generated code to set up the service vtable/shims.
requirements: service must point to writable, allocated ProtobufCService storage.
descriptor must point to a valid ProtobufCServiceDescriptor.
destroy must be a valid function pointer for destroying the service (nullability not specified; behavior if NULL is unknown).

functions.name: protobuf_c_service_invoke_internal
functions.signature: void protobuf_c_service_invoke_internal(ProtobufCService *service, unsigned method_index, const ProtobufCMessage *input, ProtobufCClosure closure, void *closure_data);
functions.description: Internal helper to dispatch a service call by method index, passing the input message and a closure to receive the response.
requirements: service must point to a valid initialized ProtobufCService.
method_index should refer to an existing method (0 <= method_index < service->descriptor->n_methods).
input should point to a valid message of the correct input type for the method.
closure should be a valid callback function pointer to receive the response (nullability not specified).
closure_data is passed through to the closure unchanged.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces NUL-terminated strings suitable for FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# and filenames for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME. The fuzz stubs here only consume
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR to look up names in descriptors. Descriptors created by the
# stubs are marked invalid, so lookups will likely return NULL. Nevertheless,
# we generate interesting, valid C strings that could match typical enum/field
# or method names, including edge cases and a mix of cases, underscores, dots,
# package qualifiers, and numeric suffixes. The output is a single bytes buffer
# that may contain one or multiple NUL-terminated strings concatenated; the
# harness can slice as needed.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

IDENT_START = string.ascii_letters + "_"
IDENT_BODY = IDENT_START + string.digits

COMMON_TERMS = [
    "id", "name", "value", "status", "count", "index", "type", "code",
    "message", "input", "output", "method", "enum", "field", "package",
    "short_name", "c_name", "deprecated", "packed", "oneof",
]

ENUM_STYLE_PREFIXES = ["E", "Enum", "Error", "Status", "Kind", "Mode"]
FIELD_STYLE_PREFIXES = ["f", "field", "opt", "req", "rep", "has"]
SERVICE_STYLE_PREFIXES = ["Get", "Set", "List", "Create", "Update", "Delete", "Stream"]
PACKAGES = [
    "", "test", "example", "foo.bar", "company.product", "proto", "pkg",
]


def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 24) -> str:
    L = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = rng.choice(IDENT_START)
    if L > 1:
        s += "".join(rng.choice(IDENT_BODY) for _ in range(L - 1))
    return s


def _camel_case(parts: List[str]) -> str:
    if not parts:
        return ""
    head = parts[0]
    tail = [p[:1].upper() + p[1:] if p else "" for p in parts[1:]]
    return head + "".join(tail)


def _enum_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Enum value names often are UPPER_SNAKE or CamelCase
    style = rng.choice(["UPPER", "CAMEL", "MIX"])
    base = rng.choice(COMMON_TERMS)
    suffix_num = rng.choice(["", str(rng.randint(0, 9)), str(rng.randint(10, 999))])
    pref = rng.choice(ENUM_STYLE_PREFIXES)
    if style == "UPPER":
        parts = [pref, base, suffix_num]
        parts = [p for p in parts if p]
        return "_".join(parts).upper()
    elif style == "CAMEL":
        parts = [pref.lower(), base.lower()]
        if suffix_num:
            parts.append(suffix_num)
        return _camel_case(parts)
    else:
        # Mix underscores and camel
        a = _camel_case([pref.lower(), base.lower()])
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            a += "_" + _rand_ident(rng, 1, 5)
        if suffix_num:
            a += suffix_num
        return a


def _field_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Field names tend to be lower_snake or camelCase
    style = rng.choice(["snake", "camel"])
    parts = [rng.choice(FIELD_STYLE_PREFIXES), rng.choice(COMMON_TERMS)]
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        parts.append(rng.choice(["id", "idx", "num", "flag"]))
    if style == "snake":
        return "_".join(p.lower() for p in parts)
    return _camel_case([p.lower() for p in parts])


def _method_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Methods are often RPC-like with VerbNoun pattern
    verb = rng.choice(SERVICE_STYLE_PREFIXES)
    noun = _rand_ident(rng, 3, 10)
    return verb + noun[:1].upper() + noun[1:]


def _qualified(rng: random.Random, base: str) -> str:
    pkg = rng.choice(PACKAGES)
    if not pkg:
        return base
    return pkg + "." + base


def _edge_cases() -> List[str]:
    # Include special edge case names and empty
    return [
        "",  # empty string (valid C NUL string)
        "_", "__", "a", "Z",  # tiny identifiers
        "field", "value", "name",  # common
        "method", "input", "output",
        "Status_OK", "STATUS_UNKNOWN", "Error_NotFound",
        "get", "set", "list", "create", "delete",
        "short_name", "c_name", "package",
        # Qualified names
        "foo.bar.Baz", "example.Service.Method", "pkg.Message.field",
    ]


def _make_string_set(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    out: List[bytes] = []
    # Edge cases first to seed the corpus
    for s in _edge_cases():
        out.append(s.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00")
    # Generate themed names that might match descriptors
    for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 10)):
        out.append(_enum_name(rng).encode("utf-8") + b"\x00")
    for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 10)):
        out.append(_field_name(rng).encode("utf-8") + b"\x00")
    for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 10)):
        out.append(_method_name(rng).encode("utf-8") + b"\x00")
    # Qualified variants
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        base = _rand_ident(rng, 3, 12)
        out.append(_qualified(rng, base).encode("utf-8") + b"\x00")
    # Random identifiers and mixed case
    for _ in range(rng.randint(6, 14)):
        ident = _rand_ident(rng, 1, 24)
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            ident = ident.upper()
        elif rng.random() < 0.6:
            ident = ident.lower()
        out.append(ident.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00")
    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    chunks = _make_string_set(rng)
    # Shuffle to increase coverage across calls
    rng.shuffle(chunks)
    data = b"".join(chunks)
    # Ensure within limit
    if len(data) > MAX_TOTAL:
        data = data[:MAX_TOTAL]
        # Guarantee last string is NUL-terminated
        if data[-1:] != b"\x00":
            # Truncate back to last NUL if present, else append NUL if room
            lastnul = data.rfind(b"\x00")
            if lastnul == -1:
                data = data[:-1] + b"\x00"
            else:
                data = data[: lastnul + 1]
    return data
